summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, failed kidney transplant, and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, was admitted with fever and rigors. She was found to be septic with E. coli bacteremia. Initial workup included CT and MRI showing biliary dilation and a pancreatic cyst, prompting an endoscopic ultrasound which ruled out biliary obstruction but confirmed a 1.9 cm pancreatic cyst. Urine cultures were negative, and a tagged white blood cell scan showed no clear infection source. Infectious disease suspected a cyst infection given her immunocompromised state and history. She was treated with IV ceftazidime during dialysis sessions after stopping broad-spectrum antibiotics. Her fevers resolved, and she remained stable. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response occurred but resolved with rate control. Warfarin was held initially but restarted. She was discharged home to complete a three-week course of antibiotics with close outpatient follow-up.
problems: Septicemia due to escherichia coli [E. coli]
